problem: The sentence 'A full, slow profile has a large mass deficit compared with its momentum deficit, so H is high' contradicts the next sentence and the standard textbooks. In boundary-layer language a 'full' profile (velocity rising quickly near the wall) is the one with LOW H; H is high only when the profile is thin/less full near the wall (laminar). As written, a student reads that full means high H, then two lines later reads that fuller means lower H.
fix: Replace with: 'A profile that stays slow over most of the layer (laminar) has a large mass deficit compared with its momentum deficit, so H is high. A fuller profile near the wall, as in turbulent flow, has lower H.'

problem: 'Using the displacement integrand gives a wrong value, often about twice too large' is only safe for the linear profile (0.5δ against 0.25δ, exactly twice). For the 1/7 power law the displacement integrand gives 0.125δ, which is SMALLER than the true δE = 0.175δ, so the 'twice too large' claim is misleading.
fix: Say: 'For the linear profile this gives 0.5δ instead of 0.25δ, exactly twice too large; for the 1/7 power law it gives 0.125δ instead of 0.175δ. Either way the number is wrong, so use the correct integrand.'
